title: Existence of the exceptional inverse image
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Let $X,Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-morphism ([sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]). Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ be admissible: $A$ is a finite commutative ring killed by a power of $\ell$, and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. Use the pro-étale coefficient categories and $\Dctf$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and the localizing closures of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For a chosen compactification $f=p\circ j$, with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ proper ([sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]), let $Rf_!$ be the restriction of $Rp_*D(j_!)$ to these closures, with the module-object coefficient convention of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek]. Then the exact coproduct-preserving functor
$$
Rf_!:\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))\longrightarrow\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))
$$
has an exact right adjoint
$$
f^!:\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))\longrightarrow\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda)),\qquad
\Hom(Rf_!M,N)\simeq\Hom(M,f^!N),
$$
naturally for every $M\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ and $N\in\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))$. It is unique up to a unique isomorphism compatible with the adjunction, and it preserves arbitrary set-indexed direct sums.

proof.text: Apply sk-lem-brown-hypotheses to X and Y with p = ringChar k. Install the triangulated, locally small and coproduct structures it supplies. Finite type over Spec k makes Y quasi-compact, and separatedness over this affine base makes Y quasi-separated. Apply det-sf-comp-coherence-single to the supplied boundary compactification c; its first clause gives the membership witness h and its last clause preserves the constructible finite-Tor property. The ambient triangulated instance restricts through ObjectProperty.isTriangulated_lift to the canonical localizingLowerShriek F. No new compactification is chosen.

Use det-def-localizing-closure-existence for the ambient small coproducts and the localizing closure property. The latter implies closure under existing discrete colimits indexed in the object universe. Reindex through Discrete (ULift I) to get closure in the Brown indexing universe u+1. Thus inclusion of the source full subcategory preserves these coproducts. Likewise reindex the ambient preservation clause of det-sf-comp-coherence-single through the final ULift equivalence. Composition preserves these colimits, and the fully faithful target inclusion reflects them, giving preservation by F.

Essential smallness of the constructible finite-Tor property and local smallness of its inclusion into the localizing category give a small model IX equivalent to its full subcategory. Its objects belong to the closure by the defining intersection. Apply the any-small-model clause of sk-lem-brown-hypotheses to get compact generators. Apply lem-pc-brown-hom-representability-locally-small to F: every Hom(F(-),N) is representable. The Mathlib partial-adjoint criterion assembles these witnesses into F.IsLeftAdjoint, hence a right adjoint G and adjunction adj. This is the existing universe-transfer form of Brown representability, not an additional geometric assertion.

Equip G with adj.rightAdjointCommShift, the canonical coherent shift structure constructed by transposing the shifted counit. adj.commShift_of_leftAdjoint provides unit/counit compatibility. Apply lem-sf-triangulated-right-adjoint to obtain exactness. For any second adjunction F adjoint to J take adj.rightAdjointUniq adjJ. Its counit identity gives the required equation. Injectivity of (adjJ.homEquiv _ _).symm gives equality of each component of any other counit-compatible isomorphism; natural-transformation and isomorphism extensionality give uniqueness.

Transport compactness along source isomorphisms by conjugating the direct-sum Hom comparison; this is proved directly with DirectSum.map and Iso.homFromEquiv. Apply the Brown any-small-model clause on Y as well. Essential surjectivity of both small models therefore makes every constructible finite-Tor object compact in its localizing category. The shifted source model objects remain constructible finite-Tor by the thick-property clause of sk-lem-brown-hypotheses, and F takes them to constructible finite-Tor objects by det-sf-comp-coherence-single. Index this compact test family by IX times ULift Z.

Prove that the shifted generator family detects isomorphisms. For a map f bijective on all shifted-generator Hom groups, shift adjunction transports bijectivity to target shifts of f. Complete f to a distinguished triangle A to B to D to A[1]. Triangle Hom exactness first uses injectivity for f[1] to make any shifted-generator map into D have zero boundary, then surjectivity for f to make that map zero. Shift adjunction converts this to vanishing of Hom(E i,D[n]). Coproduct extensionality and the weak-generator property from sk-lem-brown-hypotheses imply IsZero D, including for an empty family. lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero gives IsIso f. Apply the proved generic lem-sc-compact-tests-right-adjoint-coproducts with the compact test family and this detection proof. Its adjunction/direct-sum comparison calculation proves preservation of every small coproduct by G, including the empty one.
